Name: Protected business intent
Requirement: Preserve declared protected names and exact counts; obtain approval for conflicting physical mappings.
Example: Keep two requested domains instead of adding a third for a sizing target.

Name: Explicit execution authorization
Requirement: Require separate explicit authorization for workspace access, writes, publication, and cleanup.
Example: An offline model request does not permit catalog creation.

Name: Owned products and row grain
Requirement: Declare a business purpose, row grain, role, classification, steward, and business uniqueness for every product.
Example: A claim line is one service line, not one claim.

Name: Current scope completeness
Requirement: Cover required current processes without speculative objects or arbitrary column padding.
Example: A reduced core retains complete surviving entities.

Name: Scoped sizing policies
Requirement: Treat sizing bands and division ratios as scoped advisory policies; do not silently trim or expand protected intent.
Example: A one-domain lookup slice need not invent operational divisions.

Name: Physical identifier integrity
Requirement: Declare valid snake-case physical names and reject scoped duplicates or mapping drift.
Example: Logical service_date maps exactly to physical service_date in the default profile.

Name: Semantic naming conventions
Requirement: Use meaningful context and units without redundant prefixes; word-count and length policies are advisory.
Example: Use rendering_provider_id and amount_usd rather than fk1 and value.

Name: Explicit SQL types and precision
Requirement: Use supported explicit primitive SQL types in enterprise_core and require DECIMAL precision and scale for declared monetary attributes.
Example: A billed amount is DECIMAL(18,2), not DOUBLE.

Name: Boolean consistency
Requirement: Use a consistent declared boolean representation and review name-based type proposals.
Example: BOOLEAN flags have no text regex.

Name: Separate enums and format patterns
Requirement: Separate STRING format patterns from allowed values; promote categories beyond the configured inline cap to references.
Example: Six inline values pass; seven require a reference entity under the default policy.

Name: Declared primary and business keys
Requirement: Declare a nonempty PK tuple of existing non-null attributes and explicit business uniqueness tuples.
Example: A composite PK preserves ordered columns rather than guessing from suffixes.

Name: Resolved FK endpoints
Requirement: Resolve every FK tuple to an existing target product's exact declared PK tuple.
Example: claim.line.header_id references claim.header.header_id.

Name: Exact key tuple types
Requirement: Require exact source/target types and tuple arity for declared FKs.
Example: BIGINT references BIGINT; DECIMAL scale differences are not ignored.

Name: Relationship contract
Requirement: Declare role, cardinality, optionality, justification, provenance, and population phase for every relationship.
Example: A child awaiting its parent uses a nullable FK and documented later enrichment.

Name: Distinct relationship roles
Requirement: Use distinct business-role labels for multiple FKs to one target; never wire a PK tuple to itself.
Example: Billing and rendering provider roles are distinct.

Name: Business relationship review
Requirement: Verify relationship meaning, many-side ownership, process coverage, and genuine M:N reciprocity through architect review.
Example: Provider participation owns network membership dates.

Name: Declared graph policy
Requirement: Apply the declared graph policy; exclude only explicitly justified hierarchy self-edges from default cycle checks.
Example: parent_provider_id is distinct from provider_id and has hierarchy justification.

Name: Purposeful connectivity
Requirement: Require purposeful connectivity or explicit standalone scope justification; never invent joins to fix a silo metric.
Example: An incoming-only status lookup is connected.

Name: Evidence-based normalization
Requirement: Review determinants and dependencies while retaining event snapshots, audit evidence, source reconciliation, and distinct semantics.
Example: unit_price_at_service remains beside provider_id.

Name: Conservative semantic deduplication
Requirement: Propose merges/removals only after comparing grain, lifecycle, ownership, dependencies, and authoritative source.
Example: Method and channel are not duplicates.

Name: Descriptions and glossary
Requirement: Require substantive descriptions and glossary terms, ownership and semantic subdomain assignments.
Example: Every applicable attribute has a glossary term, not just 90 percent.

Name: Declared sensitivity policy
Requirement: Require explicit sensitivity classification and markers for declared sensitive fields; classify unmarked candidates through review.
Example: An explicitly personal date_of_birth is restricted with sensitivity=personal.

Name: Structured governance metadata
Requirement: Keep tags structured and nonstructural; preserve requested metadata and applicable standards without claiming legal compliance.
Example: PK declarations are not classification tags; a HIPAA tag is not certification.

Name: Industry taxonomy and editorial policy
Requirement: Apply approved taxonomy and editorial width policies rather than universal department or description limits.
Example: A canonical industry division can override operations/business/corporate.

Name: Single-source metric dependencies
Requirement: Declare at least one dimension and measure with real single-source dependencies in the MVP supported expression set.
Example: SUM(paid_amount) preserves DECIMAL semantics.

Name: Business metric intent
Requirement: Preserve named KPI intent, count, grain, category casing, and zero-denominator behavior; keep projections outside core stored KPIs.
Example: Denial_rate compares the documented lowercase denied value.

Name: Canonical representation parity
Requirement: Keep delivered SQL and DBML identical to deterministic canonical example representations.
Example: PK/FK types and names agree across model and derivatives.

Name: Immutable versioned evolution
Requirement: Preserve source snapshots and version changes with dependency and consumer impact; do not overwrite input.
Example: A rename updates FK targets and metric dependencies in a new version.

Name: Honest evidence levels
Requirement: Report structured evidence and distinguish static, workspace, physical, and data levels without success-shaped fallbacks.
Example: Physical checks are not_run after an offline review.

Name: Requirement accounting
Requirement: Account for every applicable requirement with existing object targets and mapped checks; retain manual and blocked items.
Example: A manual business-meaning review stays unverified in static coverage.

Name: Bounded repair proposals
Requirement: Stop on unresolved conflicts and present bounded repairs rather than automatic deletion or unlimited retry.
Example: A protected cyclic link produces a proposal instead of being removed.

Name: Future sample integrity
Requirement: If later authorized, generate deterministic business-appropriate samples using actual parent keys and constraint checks.
Example: FK values come from the generated parent pool, not guessed ranges.

Name: Versioned artifact contracts
Requirement: Conform to the versioned canonical JSON and report schemas; reject undocumented or malformed fields.
Example: A string-valued nullable flag is invalid.

Name: Standalone package integrity
Requirement: Keep required package files, metadata, links, source dispositions, and assets complete and resolvable.
Example: Both duplicate source IDs retain their distinct source-line mappings.

Name: Source occurrence traceability
Requirement: Account for every source occurrence with an explicit disposition and valid canonical target where applicable.
Example: Incomplete ATT-RUL-069 maps to the corroborated enum policy without inventing missing text.

Name: Common product shape by default
Requirement: Compare every designed or supplied product with its class's common form: PK first, FKs clustered, typed columns, and no embedded entities, repeating groups, or EAV. Remodel anti-patterns and report band deviations as advice.
Example: A flat claim table with member_name/member_phone and diagnosis_code_1..3 becomes a member master plus a claim_diagnosis child.
